description: Discover business leads and contacts directly from authors who recently published LinkedIn posts matching specific keywords. Unlike precept_search_leads (which searches by persona query), this tool discovers leads directly from content authors without requiring a persona query. Each result is one post author (a lead), not a raw post: full_name, first_name, last_name, job_title, company_name, company_domain, linkedin, user_name, location, country, connections_count, followers, enrich_email / enrich_phone ('Not Found' unless includeContactDetails), plus a post object with url, content (truncated to 2000 characters), posted_at, likes_count and comments_count. findInsights adds summary, top_problems, internal_strategic_initiatives and public_appearances. Results come back in relevance order by default; pass sortBy 'likes' or 'comments' to get the most-engaged posts instead (Precept selects the top posts by that metric from a larger candidate pool, then returns them in descending order). Results depend heavily on the timeframe (past 24 hours, week or month), so if the user hasn't said which, it's worth asking. Short keywords of 1 to 3 words (e.g. ['SEO problem', 'struggling with SEO']) match far more posts than long sentences. Returns 30 leads by default; pass limit for more (max 1000). Uses credits (from 5.1 per lead); precept_check_credits shows the balance. Runs asynchronously and returns an enrichment_id (jobId). Check progress with precept_get_job_status; jobs can take up to about 10 minutes, so checking every ~4 seconds for up to about 150 checks before treating a job as stalled gives the best experience, with a brief progress update to the user every minute or so. Results work well as a table. Users often follow up by asking for more leads or for emails and phone numbers via precept_enrich_leads.

description.description: A clear, detailed description of what the user is searching for (e.g. 'Founders discussing AI workflow automation or marketing challenges'). This provides context for relevance evaluation.

enrichType.description: Type of contact details to find. Options: 'emails' (+1 credit/lead), 'phones' (+10 credits/lead). Default: both (+11 credits/lead). Only used when includeContactDetails is true.

findInsights.description: Generate AI insights for each lead including professional summary, top problems, internal strategic initiatives, and public appearances. Costs 1.1 credits per lead if true, 0.1 credits if false. Default: false.

includeContactDetails.description: Whether to find and verify email addresses and phone numbers for discovered authors. Adds +1 credit for email, +10 for phone (or +11 for both) per person. Contact details add significant cost, so enable this when the user asks for emails or phone numbers.

keywords.description: 1 to 5 concise keywords or phrases to search LinkedIn posts for (e.g. ['SEO problem', 'struggling with SEO'] or ['AI workflow', 'marketing automation']). Keep phrases short (1-3 words) to maximize search recall. Avoid full sentences or conversational filler.

limit.description: Maximum number of leads to return (max 1000). Defaults to 30.

location.description: Optional target location/country to filter post authors by (e.g. 'United States', 'US', 'UK', 'Canada'). Filters authors by verified profile location/country in real-time.

name.description: A readable name for this enrichment job, used for searching on the Precept dashboard.

sortBy.description: How to rank posts: 'relevance' (default), 'likes' (most-liked posts first) or 'comments' (most-commented posts first). Sorting by likes/comments picks the top posts by that metric from a larger candidate pool, so it changes which leads are returned, not just their order. No extra cost.

streamingResults.description: Optional. When true (and webhookUrl is provided), contact results are progressively streamed to the webhook as each lead is enriched.

timeframe.description: Timeframe of LinkedIn posts to search: '24h' (past 24 hours), 'week' (past week), 'month' (past month), or 'year' (past year). 'day' is also accepted for backward compatibility.

webhookUrl.description: Optional webhook URL to receive enrichment results. NOTE: NOT needed for MCP assistant workflows. You can omit this and use precept_get_job_status with the returned enrichment_id to fetch the results directly.

name: precept_get_leads_from_post_search

outputSchema.description: Initialization response containing the jobId to poll for results

enrichment_id.description: The unique job ID to poll with precept_get_job_status

finalLimit.description: Adjusted limit based on available credit balance

message.description: Status message describing the initialized job

title: Leads from LinkedIn Posts
